rules.title: while condition must be bool
rules.statement: In `while COND { ... }`, COND must have type `bool` (or be an error type); any other type is a type error.

rules.title: while body does not establish definite assignment
rules.statement: A `while`/`while let` loop may execute zero times, so assignments/initializations performed in its body do not count as definitely-initialized in the enclosing scope; the definite-assignment state is restored to its pre-loop value on every exit path.

rules.title: loop label attaches to the while loop itself
rules.statement: A leading loop label `'a:` on a `while`/`while let` binds to that loop (added to the active-label set for its body) and is consumed before lowering the body, so an unlabeled nested loop inside the body cannot capture it; `break 'a` / `continue 'a` inside the body resolve to the labeled loop.

rules.title: while body is in loop context
rules.statement: Statements in a `while`/`while let` body execute in loop context (loop depth incremented, a break-frame pushed), so `break` and `continue` are permitted there and resolve to this loop.

rules.title: while-let desugars to loop + match
rules.statement: `while let PAT = EXPR { BODY }` is equivalent to `loop { match EXPR { PAT => { BODY }, _ => break } }`: the loop continues while EXPR matches PAT (binding PAT each iteration), and terminates the first time it does not.

rules.title: while-let pattern bindings scope over body
rules.statement: Bindings introduced by the `while let` pattern are in scope only within the loop body (a fresh scope is pushed for the matched arm and popped after the body).

rules.title: while-let trailing chain condition must be bool
rules.statement: In a `while let PAT = EXPR && COND` chain, the trailing condition COND must have type `bool` (or error); it is evaluated with the pattern's bindings in scope and folded into the match-arm guard so the loop continues only when the pattern matches AND COND holds.

rules.title: while-let chain condition cannot reference nested enum-variant bindings
rules.statement: A `while let` chain trailing condition may not reference bindings introduced by a nested enum-variant subpattern of the same pattern; such a reference is an error (match in the body instead).
rules.uncertainty: Stated as a current implementation limitation ('cannot yet'); likely a temporary divergence rather than an intended language rule.

rules.title: multi-segment while-let chain desugars to nested if-let-else-break
rules.statement: A multi-segment let-chain `while let P1 = e1 && (let P2 = e2 | cond) && ... { BODY }` desugars to `loop { { if let P1 = e1 { { if let P2 = e2 { ... BODY ... } else { break; } } } else { break; } } }`, building inside-out so each segment (a `let PAT = VALUE` or a boolean condition) wraps the running body and falls to `break` on failure; a chain requires at least 2 segments.
examples: while let Some(a) = x.next() && let Some(b) = y.next() { f(a, b); }

rules.title: while loop maps to its header source line
rules.statement: The emitted `while` loop is attributed to the source line of the `while` keyword (the loop header), not the last line of its body, for debug/stepping purposes.
